subject: science
intro: Some chemical reactions release thermal energy (they warm their surroundings); these are exothermic. Other reactions absorb thermal energy (they cool their surroundings); these are endothermic. Engineers use these reactions to design devices. A hand warmer uses an exothermic reaction to release heat. An instant cold pack uses an endothermic reaction to absorb heat and feel cold. When designing such a device, engineers test it and modify it to control how much heat is released or absorbed and how long it lasts.

items.prompt: A hand warmer gets hot when activated. Is the reaction inside exothermic or endothermic?

steps: The hand warmer releases heat to its surroundings.
A reaction that releases thermal energy is exothermic.

items.prompt: An instant cold pack feels cold when squeezed. Is its reaction exothermic or endothermic, and why?

steps: The cold pack absorbs heat from its surroundings, making them feel cold.
A reaction that absorbs thermal energy is endothermic.

items.prompt: An engineer builds a warming device but it does not get hot enough. Name one way they might modify the design.

steps: The device needs to release more thermal energy.
The engineer could increase the amount of reactants in the exothermic reaction.
Testing the new version shows if it now gets hot enough.
solution.answer: Use more reactant so the exothermic reaction releases more heat, then retest.

steps: An exothermic reaction releases thermal energy to its surroundings.
An endothermic reaction absorbs thermal energy from its surroundings.

items.prompt: Why do engineers test and modify a device design?

steps: Testing and modifying lets them improve how well the device works.
solution.answer: To improve how well it works.
